# ardopcf (ARDOP modem) — bundled as a separate executable

[ardopcf](https://github.com/pflarue/ardop) by Rick Muething, John Wiseman
and Peter LaRue is the open ARDOP modem Winlink gateways accept. POTACAT
launches it only for a Winlink ARDOP session and talks to it through Pat over
its loopback host port — never linked.

- License: MIT (`LICENSE`, copied from the pinned tag)
- Pinned: see `VERSION.txt`. Upstream has stopped development; this is a
  fixed, known-good version.
- Windows and Linux only: ardopcf has no macOS (CoreAudio) backend.
- Built by `scripts/build-winlink-helpers.sh` (make; MSYS2 MINGW64 on
  Windows, statically linked), staged to `assets/ardopcf/`, packaged to
  `resources/bin/ardopcf[.exe]`.
- **Patched in our build** (`scripts/build-winlink-helpers.sh`): the Windows
  device-name tables are 64 entries instead of 16 and the device count is
  capped at 64. Upstream copies every sound device's name into a 16-entry
  table, so a PC with SmartSDR's DAX running (~40 devices) crashed with
  0xC0000005 before opening audio. Upstream has stopped development, so the
  patch lives here.
- **Socket audio backend** (`src/SocketAudio.c` + `potacat-socket-audio.patch`,
  generated by `scripts/gen-ardopcf-patch.py` from the pinned sources): with
  both devices given as `tcp:<port>`, ardopcf opens no sound card — it takes
  the radio's receive audio from, and sends its transmit audio to, a loopback
  port POTACAT serves (12 kHz s16 mono, raw, both ways). POTACAT carries that
  over Flex Direct, Icom Network or its own sound device, so no DAX program
  or virtual cable is needed (K3SBP 2026-10-22: DAX TX took no audio at all).
  The backend has no platform audio code, so a macOS ardopcf becomes possible.
- **POTACAT never gives it a PTT or CAT flag** (`-p/-c/-g/-k/-u`): it only
  reports PTT to its host, Pat keys through POTACAT's rigctld shim, and
  POTACAT keys the radio. `lib/ardop-process.js` refuses those flags.
